_comment: FOOTWEAR RUBRIC v1 (2026-07-29). Hazard space: 0 = inert, 100 = worst.
Public Toxome Score is the inverse (100 - hazard), so HIGHER = CLEANER,
matching lib/fiber-scores.json.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Shoes cannot use the apparel fiber rubric. That rubric
reads one composition string and assumes it describes the whole garment.
A shoe is an assembly: an upper, a lining, a footbed and a sole, each a
different material, and only the upper is ever quoted as a percentage.
Scoring the upper alone rated the Vivobarefoot Primus Lite Knit Natural 85
and 'low risk' while its sole is recycled polyurethane, which scores 28 on
its own. That is the failure this file corrects.
MATERIAL HAZARDS below reuse the fiber table's numbers wherever the two
overlap (wool 24, merino 10, organic cotton 8, lyocell 12, leather 40 with
a 30 vegetable-tanned floor, polyurethane 72, polyester 70, nylon 64,
elastane 63) so a wool shoe and a wool sweater cannot disagree. Materials
that only appear in footwear are new.
Component weights are skin-contact-and-mass, not surface area. The upper
and the lining are what touch skin all day; the sole is the bulk of the
plastic and the offgassing but sits under the foot behind a footbed.
Weights are renormalised over whatever components are actually disclosed,
so a shoe that states only upper and sole is scored on those two rather
than being silently credited for a lining nobody described.

thresholds._comment: Identical bands to the fiber rubric, so 67 remains the clean bar.

materials._comment: Keys are normalised: lowercase, spaces to underscores.

natural_rubber._note: Vulcanisation uses sulfur and accelerators (thiurams, carbamates), a real contact-allergen route, but it is not a petroleum polymer and does not shed microplastic.

leather._note: Floor unlocks on stated vegetable tanning. Chrome tanning is the exposure that matters here, so tanning is a pillar rather than a footnote.

hotmelt._note: Thermoplastic adhesive, usually polyurethane or polyamide. Solid and largely bound once cured, so below a structural plastic but not inert.

eva._note: Ethylene-vinyl acetate foam. A plastic, and it does abrade, but relatively inert and not a known endocrine route, so it sits below polyurethane.

polyurethane._note: Includes recycled PU. Recycling changes the feedstock, not what the material does against skin, so it scores the same. Same call the fiber rubric makes on recycled polyester.

mirum._note: MIRUM (Natural Fiber Welding): plant-based leather alternative of natural rubber, plant oils, minerals and plant fibers. Brand-stated as containing no synthetics or plastic. Priced with natural rubber, which is its binder.

synthetic_rubber._note: SBR/BR and friends. A petroleum polymer, so well above natural rubber, but a cured solid rather than a foam and not a known endocrine route, so below polyurethane.

pla._note: Polylactic acid. Bio-based and compostable in industrial conditions, but still a thermoplastic against skin.

_comment: Additive hazard, applied after the weighted component blend and capped in
total by constants.modifierCap. Only applied when the brand STATES the
thing. An undisclosed treatment is recorded in `missing`, never guessed.

waterproof_membrane._note: Durable water repellency is the main PFAS route in footwear.

waterproof_pfc_free._note: Brand states PFC/PFAS-free. Still a coating, but not the fluorinated one.

antimicrobial_treatment._note: Silver or triclosan finishes, applied to the part held against skin.

solvent_cemented._note: Solvent-based cement construction. Only applied when stated; most brands never say, so this is usually absent rather than zero.
